title: Reading
description: Four novels and four complete Song ci poems by Su Shi, Chen Yuyi, Wang Anshi, and Li Qingzhao.
heading: A few pages worth keeping.

sections.heading: Ordinary lives, closely read.
sections.intro: A starting shelf of stories about companionship, loss, and the possibility of beginning again. These short introductions leave room for personal notes to come.

books.title: The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry
books.author: Rachel Joyce
books.blurb: A retired man goes out to post a letter and keeps walking. The journey gives old regrets a physical shape: distance, tired feet, unexpected company. A good place to begin for readers drawn to an unhurried story about what people carry, and what they might still put down.
books.sourceLabel: About the book · Penguin Random House
books.reflection: It brought me back to reading after three years of numbness, and helped carry me through a difficult stretch of life.

books.title: A Man Called Ove
books.originalTitle: 《一个叫欧维的男人决定去死》
books.author: Fredrik Backman
books.blurb: Ove has rules for almost everything, and little patience for the neighbours who keep breaking them. Beneath the friction sits a story about grief and the practical ways people look after one another. For readers who enjoy humour with tenderness just below the surface.
books.reflection: It helped me face what life gives and takes away with a little more steadiness.

books.title: My Grandmother Asked Me to Tell You She’s Sorry
books.author: Fredrik Backman
books.blurb: A grandmother’s letters send seven-year-old Elsa into the complicated lives of her neighbours. Fairy tales and ordinary rooms gradually begin to overlap. For readers interested in how stories can make unfamiliar people more understandable, without making them less strange.
books.reflection: It moved me in a way no other book has ever quite replaced.

books.title: The Storied Life of A.J. Fikry
books.author: Gabrielle Zevin
books.blurb: A bookseller’s shrinking world opens unexpectedly around a small island bookshop. Books here become a way to find company and pass something on. A natural next read for anyone who likes stories in which a place, and the people who gather there, matter as much as the plot.
books.reflection: It gave me the courage to begin again.

readingPaths.title: Journeys & second chances
readingPaths.description: A letter takes Harold onto the road; an unexpected arrival opens A.J. Fikry’s closed-off life. Two different ways of beginning again.
bookTitles: The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry
The Storied Life of A.J. Fikry

readingPaths.title: Neighbours & chosen family
readingPaths.description: In Backman’s two novels, new neighbours and a grandmother’s letters draw separate lives together: shared buildings, unlikely friendships, and care across generations.
bookTitles: My Grandmother Asked Me to Tell You She’s Sorry

readingPaths.title: Stories we pass on
readingPaths.description: A grandmother’s invented kingdoms and a bookseller’s shared stories connect generations. Then turn from fiction to Song ci: another way into memory, history, and culture.
bookTitles: My Grandmother Asked Me to Tell You She’s Sorry
The Storied Life of A.J. Fikry

excerpts.text:
夜饮东坡醒复醉，
归来仿佛三更。
家童鼻息已雷鸣。
敲门都不应，
倚杖听江声。

长恨此身非我有，
何时忘却营营？
夜阑风静縠纹平。
小舟从此逝，
江海寄馀生。
excerpts.author: Su Shi · 苏轼
excerpts.work: 临江仙 · 夜饮东坡醒复醉
excerpts.sourceLabel: Chinese text · 唐宋名家词选
excerpts.context: Written during Su Shi’s exile in Huangzhou, this lyric opens with a late return from drinking at Dongpo. The anthology glosses yingying as the pursuit of status and profit. The final lines turn to a small boat and a wish to entrust the remaining years to rivers and seas.
excerpts.contextSourceLabel: Background notes · 唐宋名家词选

excerpts.text:
忆昔午桥桥上饮，
坐中多是豪英。
长沟流月去无声。
杏花疏影里，
吹笛到天明。

二十馀年如一梦，
此身虽在堪惊。
闲登小阁看新晴。
古今多少事，
渔唱起三更。
excerpts.author: Chen Yuyi · 陈与义
excerpts.work: 临江仙 · 忆昔午桥桥上饮
excerpts.sourceLabel: Chinese text · 唐宋名家词选
excerpts.context: The poem’s prefatory note describes climbing a small pavilion at night and remembering earlier days in Luoyang. The first stanza recalls drinking with companions and flute music until dawn; the second looks back across more than twenty years, ending with a fisherman’s song in the night.
excerpts.contextSourceLabel: Background notes · 唐宋名家词选

excerpts.text:
别馆寒砧，
孤城画角，
一派秋声入寥廓。
东归燕从海上去，
南来雁向沙头落。
楚台风，
庾楼月，
宛如昨。

无奈被些名利缚！
无奈被它情担阁！
可惜风流总闲却！
当初谩留华表语，
而今误我秦楼约。
梦阑时，
酒醒后，
思量着。
excerpts.author: Wang Anshi · 王安石
excerpts.work: 千秋岁引 · 别馆寒砧
excerpts.sourceLabel: Chinese text · 唐宋名家词选
excerpts.context: The anthology subtitles this lyric “Autumn Scene.” Its notes identify the opening sounds as cloth being beaten on a stone and a painted horn used in military life. Swallows and geese cross the landscape before the poem turns to the constraints of reputation, attachment, and missed promises.
excerpts.contextSourceLabel: Background notes · 唐宋名家词选

excerpts.text:
天接云涛连晓雾，
星河欲转千帆舞。
仿佛梦魂归帝所。
闻天语，
殷勤问我归何处？

我报路长嗟日暮，
学诗漫有惊人句。
九万里风鹏正举。
风休住，
蓬舟吹取三山去。
excerpts.author: Li Qingzhao · 李清照
excerpts.work: 渔家傲 · 天接云涛连晓雾
excerpts.sourceLabel: Chinese text · 唐宋名家词选
excerpts.context: This lyric takes the form of a dream journey: the speaker reaches a celestial court and is asked where she wishes to go. The closing “three mountains” are not an ordinary destination; the anthology identifies them as Fangzhang, Yingzhou, and Penglai, the three mythical mountains of immortals in the Bohai Sea.
excerpts.contextSourceLabel: Background notes · 唐宋名家词选
